prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1182; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of a multi-lane roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 moved from the adjacent lane into the path of Driver 1's vehicle during a lane change. The two vehicles sideswiped one another, and the resulting contact damage to the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle and the passenger side of Driver 2's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact angle and direction of travel. Driver 1 reported a wrist injury at the scene and was transported for evaluation. The injury described is consistent with the kind of force expected from a collision of this type. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several of the reported details, including vehicle positions and damage. No independent witnesses were identified. Responding officers and other persons on scene confirmed that Passenger was present in Driver 1's vehicle at the time of the collision. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to the reporting officer. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the applicable policy. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
